The BCM processes input signals and sends the processed data to the respective control units. It also receives data from these control units and manages the operation of various systems, including headlamps, by controlling associated functions.
The system shall receive input signals from the combination switch, process them, and send appropriate outputs to control the respective lamps.

External Lighting System shall consist of
Headlamps (Low Beam and High Beam)
Tail Lamps
Brake Lamps
Park Lamps
Daytime Running Lamps
End Marker Lamps
Side Marker Lamps
Rear Registration Plate Lamps
The BCM shall ensure that the Headlamps are non-operable when a CAN message with the IGN_15 signal value set to 0 (Ignition Off) is detected.
The BCM shall ensure that the Headlamps remain operable when a CAN message with the IGN_15 signal value set to 1 (Accessory ON), 2 (Ignition ON) is detected.
The system shall operate normally between voltage range of VtgLow= 18.5V to VtgHigh = 28.5V.
The BCM shall remain switched off when only the IGN_30 signal is detected on its designated GPIO.
Headlamp Low Beam
If the IN_SWT_LOWBEAM signal is ON, the system shall set the OUT_LAMP_LOWBEAM signal to ON via GPIO within 300ms.
If the IN_SWT_LOWBEAM signal is OFF, the system shall set the OUT_LAMP_LOWBEAM signal to OFF via GPIO within 300ms.
The system shall log a DTC B0157-15 in case of a short to battery condition for the Low Beam front left lamp.
The BCM shall go to the OFF state when a CAN message with the IGN_15 signal value set to 0 (Ignition Off) is detected.

The system shall ensure that the Low Beam headlamps remain functional when the BCM is in the ON state, which occurs when a CAN message with the IGN_15 signal value set to 1 (Accessory ON), 2 (Ignition ON) is detected.
The system shall ensure that the Low Beam headlamps are disabled when the BCM is in the OFF state, which occurs when a CAN message with the IGN_15 signal value set to 0 (Ignition Off) is detected.
The system shall monitor IN_SWT_LOWBEAM signal on GPIO when in on state
If the IN_SWT_LOWBEAM signal is ON, the system shall set the OUT_LAMP_LOWBEAM signal to ON via GPIO (Relay Operation).
If the IN_SWT_LOWBEAM signal is OFF, the system shall set the OUT_LAMP_LOWBEAM signal to OFF via GPIO (Relay Operation).
The system shall log a DTC B0257-15 in case of a short to battery condition for the Low Beam front right lamp.
The system shall log a DTC B0157-11 in case of a short to ground condition for the Low Beam front left lamp.
The system shall log a DTC B0257-11 in case of a short to ground condition for the Low Beam front right lamp.
The system shall log a DTC B0157-00 in case of a short to open condition for the Low Beam front left lamp.
The system shall log a DTC B0257-00 in case of a short to open condition for the Low Beam front right lamp.
If the IN_SWT_LOWBEAM signal is ON, the system shall set the OUT_TT_LOWBEAM signal value to 01 via CAN.
If the IN_SWT_LOWBEAM signal is OFF, the system shall set the OUT_TT_LOWBEAM signal value to 00 via CAN.
The LED used for telltale shall have following specifications
The LED shall operate at a rated power of 20mA and a voltage of 24V DC.
The LED used shall provide a luminous flux of 2 to 5 lumens
The tell tale shall be green in colour

H4 Bulb: The H4 bulb is a dual-filament halogen headlamp bulb, commonly used for both high and low beam functions. It provides a bright, focused light with separate filaments for each beam, ensuring optimal visibility in different driving conditions.
The H4 bulb shall provide a luminous flux of 1200 lumens for Low Beam
The H4 bulb shall operate at a rated voltage of 24 V
The H4 bulb shall operate at a rated power of 70 watts.
The H4 bulb shall have a maximum operating voltage of 28 V
The H4 bulb shall have a maximum operating current of 80 watts
Headlamp High Beam

The system shall ensure that the High Beam headlamps remain functional when the BCM is in the ON state, which occurs when a CAN message with the IGN_15 signal value set to 1 (Accessory ON) or 2 (Ignition ON) is detected.
The system shall ensure that the High Beam headlamps are disabled when the BCM is in the OFF state, which occurs when a CAN message with the IGN_15 signal value set to 0 (Ignition Off) is detected.
The system shall monitor IN_SWT_HIGHBEAM  signal on GPIO when in on state
If the IN_SWT_HIGHBEAM signal is ON, the system shall set the OUT_LAMP_HIGHBEAM signal to ON via GPIO (Relay Operation).
If the IN_SWT_HIGHBEAM signal is OFF, the system shall set the OUT_LAMP_HIGHBEAM signal to OFF via GPIO (Relay Operation).
If the IN_SWT_HIGHBEAM signal is ON, the system shall set the OUT_LAMP_HIGHBEAM signal to ON via GPIO within 300ms.
If the IN_SWT_HIGHBEAM signal is OFF, the system shall set the OUT_LAMP_HIGHBEAM signal to OFF via GPIO within 300ms.
The system shall log a DTC B1157-15 in case of a short to battery condition for the High Beam front left lamp.
The system shall log a DTC B1257-15 in case of a short to battery condition for the High Beam front right lamp.
The system shall log a DTC B1157-11 in case of a short to ground condition for the High Beam front left lamp.
The system shall log a DTC B1257-11 in case of a short to ground condition for the High Beam front right lamp.
The system shall log a DTC B1157-00 in case of a short to open condition for the High Beam front left lamp.
The system shall log a DTC B1257-00 in case of a short to open condition for the High Beam front right lamp.

The LED shall operate at a rated power of 20mA and a voltage of 24V DC.

The tell tale shall be blue in colour
Hardware Requirements for High Beam

H4 Bulb: The H4 bulb is a dual-filament halogen headlamp bulb, commonly used for both high and low beam functions. It provides a bright, focused light with separate filaments for each beam, ensuring optimal visibility in different driving conditions.
The H4 bulb shall provide a luminous flux of 1900 lumens for High Beam
The H4 bulb shall operate at a rated voltage of 24 V
The H4 bulb shall operate at a rated power of 75 watts.
The H4 bulb shall have a maximum operating voltage of 28 V
The H4 bulb shall have a maximum operating current of 85 watts
ParkLamps
If the IN_SWT_PARKLAMP signal is ON, the system shall set the OUT_LAMP_PARK signal to ON via GPIO (Relay Operation).
If the IN_SWT_PARKLAMP signal is OFF, the system shall set the OUT_LAMP_PARK signal to OFF via GPIO (Relay Operation).
If the IN_SWT_PARKLAMP signal is ON, the system shall set the OUT_LAMP_PARK signal to ON via GPIO within 300ms.
Basic Description
The system shall log a DTC B2157-00 in case of a short to open condition for the Park Lamp front left.
The system shall log a DTC B2257-00 in case of a short to open condition for the Park Lamp front right.
If the IN_SWT_PARKLAMP signal is ON, the system shall set the OUT_TT_PARK signal value to 01 via CAN.
Hardware Requirements for Park Lamps
The W5W bulb is a 24V automotive bulb commonly used for parking and position lamps. It provides low-intensity illumination
The W5W bulb shall provide a luminous flux of 50 lumens ± 20%

Park lamps, also known as position lamps, are low-intensity lights used to make a vehicle visible when parked, especially in low-light conditions. They are typically white or amber in color and are activated to indicate the vehicle's presence without fully illuminating the headlights.
Brief Description

Tail lamps are safety features that illuminate the rear of the vehicle, making it visible to other drivers. They typically consist of red lights and signal the vehicle's position, especially in low-light conditions, and may include brake lights.

The system shall ensure that the Tail Lamps remain operable when the BCM is in the ON state, which occurs when a CAN message with the IGN_15 signal value set to 1 (Accessory ON) or 2 (Ignition ON) is detected.
If both the IN_SWT_PARKLAMP AND IN_SWT_LOWBEAM signals are OFF, the system shall set the OUT_LAMP_TAIL signal to OFF via GPIO within 300ms.
The system shall log a DTC B3157-15 in case of a short to battery condition for the Tail Lamp rear left.
The system shall log a DTC B3257-15 in case of a short to battery condition for the Tail Lamp rear right.

The system shall ensure that the Park Lamps remain functional when the BCM is in the ON state, which occurs when a CAN message with the IGN_15 signal value set to 1 (Accessory ON) or 2 (Ignition ON) is detected.

P21-5W: The P21-5W is a 24V automotive bulb with a dual-filament design, used for functions like tail lamps, brake lights, and turn signals. It provides a 5W output for standard operation and up to 21W for braking or signaling, offering reliable performance in demanding environments.
The P21-5W bulb shall operate at a rated power of 5 watts.
The P21-5W bulb shall operate at a rated voltage of 24V

Brake lamps illuminate when the driver applies the brakes, signaling to other drivers that the vehicle is slowing down or stopping. Typically red, they are designed for visibility, especially in low-light conditions, to enhance safety and prevent rear-end collisions

The system shall ensure that the Brake Lamps remain operable when the BCM is in the ON state, which occurs when a CAN message with the IGN_15 signal value set to 1 (Accessory ON) or 2 (Ignition ON) is detected.

The system shall ensure that the Brake Lamps are non-operable when the BCM is in the OFF state, which occurs when a CAN message with the IGN_15 signal value set to 0 (Ignition Off) is detected.

The system shall ensure that the Brake Lamps are non-operable when the BCM is in the OFF state, which occurs when a CAN message with the IGN_15 signal value set to 1 (Accessory ON) or 2 (Ignition ON) is not detected.
The system shall ensure that the Park Lamps are disabled when the BCM is in the OFF state, which occurs when a CAN message with the IGN_15 signal value set to 0 (Ignition Off) is detected.
If the IN_SWT_BRAKE signal is OFF, the system shall set the OUT_LAMP_BRAKE signal to OFF via GPIO within 100ms.
